title: "Exercises for BST260 2026, November 9 2026"

1. Add a folder called quizzes to your bst260 github
repository.

2. Start a quarto document called `nov9.qmd` there.

3. Put your solutions to these problems in that document.
Make sure it renders.

Problem 1. Consider

```{r do1,message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(ggbeeswarm)
ggplot(pivot_longer(iris, cols=1:4), 
   aes(x=factor(name), y=value, colour=Species)) + geom_beeswarm()
```
Find thresholds on values of Petal.Length that can be used to classify
samples into species.  For example, the vector `cutsl` here
defines bins into which irises can be classified using Sepal.Length.
We can then cross-classify the species labels and the
three sepal-length based categories.
```{r lkdisc}
cutsl = c(0,5.4,6,8)
with(iris, table(cut(Sepal.Length,cutsl),Species))
```
Your job is to pick an iris feature and thresholds
on length that reduce the numbers of off-diagonal elements
of this table, which represents a "confusion matrix'.

Your answer will have the form
```
feature = "..."
cutsl = c(....)
with(iris, table(cut( ..., cutsl), Species))
```

Problem 2.

This is a crude way of estimating proportion of births
with low birth weight outcomes as it varies by mother's body weight.
```{r lklbw,message=FALSE}
library(MASS)
lm(low~I(cut(lwt,seq(0,300,50)))-1, data=birthwt)
```

Fit a two parameter model with `lm` that provides
an estimate of the proportion of births with
low birth weight outcome for women with body weight 150.
